pages.html:
Sinners, Saints and the Need for Greed

Shaun: The key to bingo is simplicity. The more simple the more popluer, its when you start toget complicated that they dont like it. Thats why there was all this mistruct when computers came in and took over instead of ball machines. Bingo customers like to think they’re very intelligent and so...

Anna: don’t we all

Shaun: absolutely! ... so if you bring in a machine that the dont understand, they’re affronted becasue they dont understand it! bingo is so simple but if you’re new to bingo its completely strange.. its something that I never came accross, but if you’re an old hand at it , you think I know what i’m doing... To make it even more complicated some of our customers play their books upside down.

Anna: I’ve seen them doing that ont he tables.

Shaun: some of them actually memorise every number on the board,

Anna: so they dont have to look at it

Shaun: they like to seem as though they really know what they ‘re doing... the most amazing thing that ever happened to me , I was calling cashline, I’d only been working there about a year, and this lady shouted, and of course on cashline they dont normally shout they press their button, on cashline its a legal requirement to press their button,

...anyway she shouted and I thought I’d better stop, and she said I’ve got a win, and I thought she’s standing in the queue, at the back of the hall for the teatime books, and I said 'but you're not playing' and she said 'I am, board 232' or whatever board it was and she had had a win, she’d put the money in and she's standing in the queues, she'd had a win! that's how serious it is, it's amazing... that was the most amazing thing that ever happened...

Anna: my name's Anna Best and I'm doing a residency here at Camden Arts Centre and this is shaun fox who've i 've invited to talk about bingo and related subjects and I've got some questions... do you want to say something about your role in the bingo hall

Shaun: I'm a manager with a company called Mecca bingo which is at the moment th e largest bingo operator in the country, we run 135 clubs up and down the country, the largest in glasgow, we do 18 thousand admissions a week in that club, eastbourne the smallest do 1500 admissions a week, and Kilburn, in the State cinema that was, so approx 3500 - 4000 admissions a week, at the gentler end of the scale... We run 14 sessions a week in most clubs, some have morning sessions, each admission is per session..

Anna: what's the diversity of customers at kilburn?
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: its shifting, it usedot be blue rinse set, old grannies filling up their time, afternoon cutomers are between 500 and 65, the evening customers are actually much younger, the average age is about 40 and people in mid thirties fits nicely in an evening,and afterwarss can still go out to a club... the majority of our customers whether young or old tends to be women

Anna: thats interesting, i spoke to people who said one of the reasons they're going there is because they dont get any hassle, they can go alone and not get hassled by men

Shaun: its considered very safe. I think thats why an awful lot of older women come to us because it is a safe place they can go... because we're governed by licensing laws, (thats changing now since the national lottery has been introduced), its regulated as to who can come in and out of the hall, we know exactly who comes ina nd out, because you have to be member (of Mecca Social Club) to play .. it is a safe haven

Anna: you can leave your bag and go off to the loo and come back, its a safe atmosphere, as well as being quite intimidating because its so big at first!

Shaun: i try to make sure that I know peoples names, i do my best, we trying to create the feeling of a social club, even the younger customers in the evening still like the fact that you know who they are...

Anna: can you talk a bit about Rank

Shaun:its a huge company, the rank organisation, mecca is just part of it, part of the Leisure and entertainment industry. everyone who joins mecca joins BECTU which is actually an entertainers and an actors union. Rank own other things like themed restaurants, Haven holiday resorts, Butlins, Pinewood Studios, and warner Cinemas

Thomas: can I just say that because we're a small audience today please feel free to ask any questions...

Tomoko: is there a condition for entry
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: yes there is, to be a member you have to be over the age of eighteen, the law says you cant game unless your over the age of eighteen...

Tomoko: no children allowed...

Andy: which is why its probably quite popular with women

Anna: they can leave the kids at home

Shaun: very true! the husbands ring up and say 'where is she?!', I cant disclose wether someone's in the building or not, its not my job to track people. It can get quite violent...The other day it happened with a woman who's a very keen bingo player and her partner came down to the club..

Andy: when you say shes a keen bingo player what you mean is she's an addicted gambler

Shaun: i dont think i could make that judgement, she may come for bingo or for the fact that she's getting out of the house... i cant say if shes addicted or not...
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Andy: if a person wins a prize do they win it as a cheque

Shaun: only the national game which could be 100,000 pounds... usually they want cash, its all cash! or prizes , tomorrow we're doing a mothers day promotion so we're having a mums day bonus prize of 500... some of the promotions are put together by our team, some our national promotions that pour company force (want!) us to do...

Anna: there's a certain amount of stuff which you can do which is your own thing, like Dave used to make up the trailers for new films every saturday, and then there's the standard company stuff,

Shaun: most large companies have a brand image, its been hard for mecca to create a brand image because some of the clubs used to be called Top Rank and the customers didn't see them when they were re-named Mecca. Rank want a more homogenous image... and so thats why we have a colour scheme inside the building, purples lilacs and blues and pink neon outside

Anna: is right you cant put the word 'bingo' outside the building
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: yes because the laws are very strict about whats called 'enticement to game'... fruit machines are considered hard gaming, and cant entice people to play they're meant to come of their own free will, because it is so addictive

Anna: the fruit machines manufacturers have a direct relationship with rank, is that right?

Shaun: absolutely yes, we have a so called development section at head office in maidenhead and they have a budget and its a huge budget to spend with the people who make fruit machines and we tell the kind of fruit machine we want.. a huge amount of money goes int researching everything down to colours noises, the flashing lights, we make a lot more money of fruit machines than bingo, fruit machines account for one third of our income and that income includes cashline, prizeline, the cafe and all the other sidelines...its huge. They're more addictive and expensive than any other form of gaming... you can put 100 into a fruit machine

Andy: which will take about half an hour!
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Anna: it is scary watching people put huge amounts of money in

Andy: how much is it to play bingo?

Shaun: bingo is actually quite expensive

Anna:you can play just one part of a page but its not much fun

Shaun: i'll give you an example but it varies, on sunday its a pound to come in for your books, cashline can be an average of 5 to 10, our bar buffets very cheap, so on a sunday night and to have ago on the fruit machines as well, you'd need 35 to 40 on a sunday night, in an afternoon its a bit cheaper, because we're catering for an older customer

Andy: so the regular keen customer who come from midday to 11.30 at night every day you mention before might be spending, 100 a day, 700 a week... not surprising her partners tapping on your door
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: mmm, there's very few places you can go and spend 10 and come away with 15,000... people who play regularly tend to break even. its expensive, but the bar is cheap, as a service for our customers, it makes a profit but not a lot.

Anna: I find very interesting about being in the bingo hall, the paradox between the sense of community and of caring and the scary addiction side of it, all the psychological states that are going on there...

Shaun: a lot of people come to us as an escape (from their husbands or whatever, its a safe haven, we consciously aim to o create this feeling... because if people are happy they will spend more money, if people feel comfortable and secure they will part with more money, the art of all sales is to sell people things they dont want

Anna: there's also the sort of glamorous aspect, like the callers used to wear glittery jackets
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: we still have dress codes... managers used to have to wear a tuxedo after 6pm, the callers still wear evening wear, some of them are outrageous, there's a caller in reading who wears glitter suit and a loud pink ruffle shirt, you've got spotlights, its meant to be entertaining, every caller has their own style, Perm's quite over the top whereas George is quite sober

Anna: and monotonous!

Shaun: women callers are not at all popular, I'm afraid! it's very tough to call, and very tough on women. You have to try and make each number sound different, you only have 90 numbers!, you have to give each one a character, you have to be on the ball, can't miss a call...the callers have a fan club because some callers have a style or the players feel they are luckier with them... they feel the caller has control over the luck, (which is not true! if your thinking of bribing a caller...)

Anna: I've got another question actuaally, which is how come the bingo sessions seem to always last the right amount of time?
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: (laughs) ooh, trade secrets! on the clallers rostrum we have a clock and the general rule is, sometimes the sessions do overrun if we have a problem or if there's a LINK game, but the golden rule is five minutes a page so they know after five mionuted they should've finished a page, which is one line tow lines and a full house... callers will change their pace to make sure that they make it on time ... at a quieter saession the laws of porbablilty mean it will take longer for someone to have a full house...so you'd probably end up calling out of ninety numbers you could end up calling sixty five... its only very unlikely that you'd take that long to get a full house... that would be very rare

Anna: so thats just probability

Shaun: nobody knows the sequence at which those numbers will be generating, althought ey think we do , they really think we do! I honestly dont know... I know what the plate number or the security sequence is... but wether or not people have a win is dependant on what numbers are generated and of thise numbers happen tobe in the right order so they get a line or a full house before anyone else, it is completeyl random

Anna: so this woman who reckons there's a winnign book out there...
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: if shes thinking we sell a set and theres one book that we know will win, beforehand, thats not true, becasue we dont... and they get even more upset if say one person wins one line two lines and a full house all togehter they think its definitely fixed. The techniology that goes into producing the bingo books is really interesting , but i wont bore you with the details, I ahve a sheet which goes into all the probabilities, and a permutation, which is a sheet of numbers on the book whoch go on a sheet of numbers when they're made, and then into different books, on the main session books there's 84,000 different permutations of numbers... on national tickets there's 96,000 and on llink ticket, which covers the whole country it's, absolutely huge (all laugh) I couldn't begin to tell you! ts more than 135,000, itcant garuntee that two people wont win, but it does garuntee that two people wont have the same security numebror the same sequence of numbers in that set... if there's a duplicate we are bound by law to pay both people the sma eamount of money , so thats why its vital we get the permutations right! ----------------

Anna: if someone wins the big prize, like £275,000 after one night do the bingo club do any publicity?
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: Yes we have run adverts in the Kilburn Times... but players are very protective, we have to ask their permission, they don't like people filming, or taking photogrpahs very much, every gaming establishemnt you ever go into and you'll notice this when you go to Las Vegas, there are never ever any windows or any clocks... there has to be no perception of time passing... no perception that people are watching you or you can see the world outside, its completely enclosed, which is why so many bingo halls are old cinemas.

Anna: you do really lose a sense of time when you're in there!

Shaun: that's what we want! and the lighting is purposelfully dim, all dim neon, which makes the fruit machines look brighter and also makes people feel a bit more secure in their anonimity, they dont like people watching him play... a lot of planning oges into where to put the AWP's the change machines

Anna: yes the fruit machines, AWP's are on the way to bingo, you have to pass through..

Thomas: Do they turn down the lights before starting a bigo session

Shaun: yes, well they're on timers...

Andy: how about temperature, do you raise it or lower it?
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: yes (laughs) and the temperature, we raise it (all laugh) all the secrets are coming out...the colours, temperature etc is all for the feling that its safe and secure, we used to use lavender perfume in the vents, now we use the vents just for extracting smoke

Anna: yes practically everyone smokes, do you think they'd stioop going to bingo if it became non smoking?

Shaun: we're lucky in kilburn we have a very high ceiling ----------

Shaun: bingo is a pastime, winners who win a lot of money, like 100,000 will come back the next night, not as you might imagine , nevr come back, bingo ids not just about winning, it's something to do...

Anna: I spoke with a player who said she doesn't event look at the prize money because she doesn't want to get buzzed up or over excited (laughs)

Shaun: it's very interesting because then ou get into why people play games... why they gamble..

Anna: is it about an excitemnet or a rush
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: i think we play on lots of different parts of people, we play on their insecurity, on the fact that we've got something they want, they come to our friendly warm atmosphere, it replaces something in their lives, they may need to win money in order to pay a bill or a debt or what have you... that's how we keep people coming to us... a 90 year old lady isn't interested in the big win, what would she do with 100,000?, for a youger person the money is probably more important... it's different motivations, but we try to play on each type of person's weaknesses, in a way, although I don't want to make it sound as if we're manipulative, we're no more manipulative than any company who's trying to sell something, we know our audience, our customers in a way that sainsburys or odeon cinemas dont, because we can track attendance, we have a database of members, we can find out which is more popular with certain age groups...

Anna: it's a club so it doesn't feel invasive that you know all those things, whereas at sainsburys it would, it does!

Shaun: exactly! I know everbody's face in the bingo hall, unlike a supermarket manager...
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Anna: do you think the things you've just been mentioning about the bingo hall, the atmosphere, the way its comforting, do you think its similar at to a church? playing on similar desires that we as individuals want to part of a community , part of a congregation...

Peter: To me, what I got, was asense of concentration, that was the only thing you could think about and everybody was thinking about the same thing, it was like going to an auction, a very strong thing sharing, couldn't think of anything else at all...

Shaun: I think to some people its more important now, for some people it will be a from of religion to them, they believe! there are some people who absolutely believe if they touch my hand they will win

a: and very superstitious

Shaun: we have a lady called Mary and she comes and visits us 14 sessions a week, she truly believes if she touches my hand she will win...

a: what do you do, hold out your hand! (laughs)

andy: surely afetr touching your hand and not winning she's going to catch on!
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: no, thats the whole point of superstition, you believe that something they had done was wrong.... she has lots of little things out on the table which she must touch in a certain order before she plays in her book. ...... I think nowadays we don't feel much sense of community, in cities, there isn't really a centre. church plays on the fact of community, of strength in numbers and solidarity.. Bingo's the same, it's a club, it's a community, it can be very regimented for some people, everyt day they sit in the same seat, sit next to the same person, leave at the same time.. For foiur hours a day we give them a bit opf fun, a sense of community, somewhere to play, and somewhere that peole know their name, ad where else can you go that people do that? It is like being part of a church, being a Catholic I'd be loath to say it's like church, but it is like a form of religion, because people believe in it, and if you believe in something then what is it? it's a faith... why do people believe in god, because they think it brings some kind of meaning to their life, purpose, direction, a guideline, something to follow, why do people come to us at Mecca, because we have a structure, a community, it gives their life a structure. For some people who come it's the only thing in their life.

Anna: I talked to someone in the bingo hall who kept saying I dont believe in this and all the while she was playing, it was so contradictory.
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed

pages.html:
Shaun: it's about not admitting that you enjoy it, men will not admit that they play bingo, because it raises questions about their masculinity, women don't like to say that they are addicted, I'm sure there are very few people who would openly admit that they are obsesed or addicted to something. That's part and parcel of your addiction is admitting that you are addicted, so they don't want to admit that. Our company chose not to have a position on Gamblers Anonymous. Managers are nopt allowed to enter into questioning the players why they come to bingo (laughs). Our job is to encourage people and not to make them question why they are there.

Anna: Do you think the belief aspect and the adduiction is about transcending or losing yourself for a while as well?

Thomas: Is it self therapeutic

Shaun: it's to escape the drudgery of their lives for some people, the lighting in the bingo hall is set at such a different rate, and its always warm but not too warm

Anna: it's soporific, it's on the edge of sleep...
pages.caption: Camden Talks: Sinners, Saints and the need for Greed
